title: Pharmacy Technician
description: Company Description As a government entity, we are dedicated to serving the public by ensuring access to essential services that foster the well-being and health of our community. Our mission is to provide high-quality healthcare services, including pharmaceutical care, with a focus on safety, efficiency, and patient satisfaction. We take pride in our commitment to upholding excellence and maintaining trust in the communities we serve. Join us in contributing to the mission of delivering accessible and reliable healthcare. Role Description This is a full-time, on-site position located in Hossana. The Pharmacy Technician will assist licensed pharmacists by preparing and dispensing medications, maintaining inventory control, organizing the pharmacy, and providing excellent customer service. Additional responsibilities include managing prescription records, ensuring compliance with applicable regulations, and working closely with other healthcare professionals to meet the needs of patients efficiently and effectively. Qualifications Strong understanding of prescriptions, and demonstrated ability in assisting with accurate preparation and dispensing of medications Background and knowledge in pharmacy operations and expertise in the scope of practice for pharmacy technicians Experience with inventory management and maintaining stock control within a pharmacy setting Excellent customer service skills and the ability to assist patients professionally and compassionately Attention to detail and strong organizational skills Ability to adhere strictly to regulatory requirements, safety standards, and ethical practices High school diploma or equivalent required; certification as a Pharmacy Technician is preferred Previous experience in a healthcare or pharmacy setting is advantageous

title: Learning Content Specialist
description: Overview People. Passion. Pride. This is what has driven our teams since 1833. Since that time, we have developed to become a critical partner in the global aviation industry, delivering time-critical logistics services at 350 locations in more than 65 countries, across six continents. But at the heart of our business is our people. Role Purpose You will support the Menzies Aviation learning teams to provide a comprehensive operational learning portfolio. Working as part of the team, you will focus on our legal, regulatory, and high-risk areas within the business, this includes all ground handling functions as governed by IATA AHM, fuelling, cargo, lounges and presentation operations. You will have in-depth knowledge of our Learning Development Policy and be and subject matter expert in the content design and development. You will work with our regional teams and coordinate with our subject matter experts across the network to ensure our portfolio is in line with regional and corporate legislation and meets both our internal and customer requirements. What You Will Be Doing Develop, update, and create learning content, ensuring input, review, and approval, from relevant internal stakeholders and subject matter experts. Maintain and update operational procedures and learning content in line with company manuals (e.g. Ground Handling Manual (GOM) and Cargo Handling Manual, (CHM)) and industry standards such as AHM, in line with business requests. Design and develop innovative learning interventions and training products. Review and challenge existing learning approaches and champion new and improved methods of learning delivery. Remain current with learning and development trends, regulatory change, and industry developments to ensure our portfolio and approach to learning remains in line with industry standards. Ensure our portfolio is accurately maintained and aligned in all learning systems. Would you like to see more detail on the accountabilities of the role? Please see the attached job description for further information. Safety, Security, Wellbeing and Compliance: You will have a responsibility and duty whilst at work to take reasonable care of the health, safety and wellbeing of yourself and others in accordance with provided information, training, and workplace health and safety rules or procedures. The company is committed to providing a safe working environment for all staff members. In all areas of our business there is a potential risk to the health, safety and welfare to everyone on our sites through the misuse of alcohol and drugs. As such the Company prohibits such misuse and carries out regular testing to enforce our Substance Misuse Policy. Please see the attached job description for further details on safety, security, wellbeing & compliance. What We Are Looking For Proficiency in Articulate 360 authoring tools. Experience with Synthesia, Vyond, Canva and/or other animation programs. At least 2 years of experience in working within a corporate training environment. Intermediate knowledge of basic computing and programmes such as, Microsoft office, project planning tools, analytical systems, and learning management systems. Ability to quickly gain a working knowledge of new technology. Diversity Menzies Aviation are a committed equal opportunity employer and encourage applications for suitably qualified and eligible applicants regardless of sex, race, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender reassignment, religion or belief, marital status, pregnancy, and maternity. We strive to create an inclusive working environment, where the different knowledge, perspectives, experiences, and approaches of our global workforce are represented. Where everyone feels valued and can reach their full potential. Please be aware that as part of our recruitment process, we may look to use a variety of resourcing tools to help us understand your skills and experience in relation to the role. Please feel free to contact to recruiter below, if there are any reasonable adjustments to our process that you would like us to consider. As part of our recruitment process, we will always consider how candidates fit with our values which you can learn more about here. Application Instructions Is this role ticking all the boxes for you? If so, please click apply now!

title: Logistics Specialist - Afrique de l’Est / Maghreb
description: Le poste sera localisé dans un de ces 5 pays sous contrat local : Addis Abeba, Ethiopie Kigali, Rwanda Rabat, Maroc Tunis, Tunisie Antananarivo, Madagascar Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI) est une association de solidarité internationale indépendante et impartiale, qui intervient dans les situations de pauvreté et d’exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Œuvrant aux côtés des personnes handicapées et vulnérabilisées, elle agit et témoigne pour répondre à leurs besoins essentiels et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Elle s’engage à promouvoir le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux. Depuis sa création en 1982, HI a mis en place des programmes de développement dans plus de 55 pays et intervient dans de nombreuses situations d’urgence. Aujourd'hui, nous avons un budget d'environ 200 millions d'euros, avec 4000 employés dans le monde. Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap. Merci d’indiquer si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement particulier, y compris pour participer aux 1ers entretiens. Retrouvez plus d’informations sur l’association : www.hi.org. CONTEXTE : Le périmètre prévu inclue principalement (mais pas uniquement) la zone géographique « CESAN » (Kenya, Ouganda, Rwanda, Sud-Soudan, Ethiopie, Somalie, RDC, Madagascar, Mozambique). Le périmètre (zones géographiques) pourra évoluer en fonction des besoins de l’organisation. Le volume d’achats annuels de CESAN est de ≃ 8M€, le nombre d’employés dans les services logistiques est de ≃ 120 La zone géographique est en cours de régionalisation, ce qui nécessite un appui particulier visant une intégration effective des pays, une optimisation des ressources, et une autonomisation forte des fonctions logistiques vis-à-vis du siège. VOTRE MISSION : Sous la responsabilité du Manager des Logistics specialists, vous, en tant que Logistics Specialist, êtes en charge de l’intégration métier et du développement des compétences de la filière métier logistique sur le terrain. Vous appuyez la qualité de la gestion de la logistique sur les programmes que vous suivez pouvant aller jusqu’à la substitution. Vous êtes un partenaire clé du développement des missions sociales et reconnu(e) pour votre valeur ajoutée auprès des programmes. Vous animez le réseau métier Logistique en assurant la formation métier, en développant des opportunités d’échanges entre pairs et jouez un rôle de coach pour l’ensemble des Regional Logistics Manager (RLM) /Country Logistics Manager (CLM) que vous accompagnez. Dans ce cadre, vos principales responsabilités seront : Développement et renforcement des capacités et compétences logistiques des programmes Contribuer à l’élaboration et au déploiement des standards Logistiques incluant LINK Assure le rôle de coach auprès des managers logistiques et accompagne les programmes dans la résolution des problèmes Animer des formations régulières (Siège et programmes) à travers l’animation d’une communauté de pratique Évaluer si les compétences requises des managers logistiques sont à la hauteur des attentes Contribuer à la diffusion des règles de conformité des bailleurs de fonds (sous l'autorité de la DFI) Contribuer au recrutement des managers logistiques Stratégie et pilotage Appuyer le Regional /Country Logistics Manager (RLM/CLM) dans le suivi de la cartographie des risques logistique des pays de son portefeuille et l’accompagner dans l’élaboration des plans d’actions correctifs et de mitigation Assurer des missions de diagnostic logistique lorsque nécessaire pouvant déboucher sur des alertes Appuyer et conseiller le RLM/CLM dans l’élaboration de la Stratégie logistique de la Stratégie opérationnelle, des plans d’action logistiques afférents par programme, et des indicateurs associés (s’assure de la pertinence des indicateurs mis en place) Sur la base du tableau de bord logistique du programme (indicateurs issus de la Stratégie opérationnelle et indicateurs communs à l’ensemble des programmes), identifier les dérives éventuelles, et les écarts par rapport aux objectifs fixés. Analyser les données contenues dans les outils et accompagne le RLM/CLM dans l’identification et le pilotage des actions correctives et communiquer les résultats auprès du Directeur de Programmes (N+1) Contrôle de la conformité et l'optimisation des programmes (tour de contrôle) Collecter les indicateurs clé de performance et fournir des analyses aux programmes et à la direction géographique Analyser les risques logistiques des programmes (fraude, vol / détournement de fonds, corruption, non-conformité, favoritisme, accidents) Alerter le Directeur logistique ou d'autres directions concernées en cas de divergences et recommande des mesures correctives Assurer le suivi du plan d'action du département logistique Garant

title: Director for Career Strategies
description: Apply now Job no: 506733 Work type: Full-Time Location: Hybrid/Flexible Work Arrangement Categories: Drexel University, Kline School of Law Job Summary The Drexel University Thomas R. Kline School of Law seeks an experienced, motivated, and creative professional to fill the position of Director for Career Strategies. The Director will be part of the School of Law’s Career Strategies Office (CSO) and will work closely with members of the CSO as well as with senior staff, faculty, and alumni of both the School of Law and the University to enhance professional opportunities for students and alumni. The Director will be responsible for student and alumni advising, developing and maintaining expertise across legal career opportunities, particularly those in the public sector, and will support the collection, analysis, and reporting of data. This position reports directly to the Associate Dean for Career Strategies. This position offers a flexible and dynamic work environment with the expectation of significant in-person engagement with the law school community. The successful candidate is expected to maintain a regular on-campus presence of at least four days per week. Essential Functions Advise students and alumni in career planning skills and job search strategies to meet the challenges of an evolving recruiting timeline and marketplace this includes: providing individualized career counseling on practice areas and employers, resume and cover letter preparation, interviewing and networking skills, and encouraging students to explore career options and engage in experiential learning. Develop and cultivate professional relationships with legal employers in the Philadelphia metropolitan area, along with regional, national, international, and other local bar associations, to increase employment opportunities for law students. Establish and maintain relationships with public sector market employers, fostering knowledge of public sector market trends, application processes and timelines, and best hiring practices for public sector career development. Collaborating with all CSO members, plan, coordinate and deliver programming on law career development and professionalism duties may include: conceptualizing, organizing and presenting educational programs and workshops that enhance students’ understanding of legal career paths, job search strategies and developing their professional identities. Manage on-campus and off-campus recruiting programs, job fairs, and networking events. Keep current and knowledgeable on employment market trends and develop strategies to enhance student employment opportunities. Develop effective working relationships with University and Law School faculty, staff, students, and alumni, along with law school partners and peer schools. Assist with collecting and entering data on students’ employment for ABA and NALP reporting. Represent the CSO and the Law School, and attend meetings and pursue committee work in local, regional, and national bar associations, NALP, and affinity groups. Assist with Admissions initiatives, where appropriate. Other duties as assigned. Required Qualifications Minimum of a Law Degree in JD from an ABA accredited law school or the equivalent combination of education and work experience (Please review the Equivalency Chart for additional information). Minimum of 3 years of experience. Preferred Qualifications Experience in a career planning office, in legal recruiting and/or law school administration is preferred. Familiarity with legal practice experience, and knowledge of career pathways in traditional and emerging legal markets in the Philadelphia metropolitan legal community is also preferred, particularly in the public sector. Additional selection criteria include: Excellent interpersonal, administrative, and leadership skills; Broad knowledge of legal career opportunities, including JD Advantage careers; Knowledge of employment trends and professional development issues in the legal profession; Excellent oral and written communication skills; The capacity to work constructively and to build effective relationships with diverse constituencies; and The ability to work both independently and in a collaborative team environment. Physical Demands Typically sitting at a desk/table Location Hybrid/Flexible Work Arrangement Additional Information This position is classified as Exempt, grade M . Compensation for this grade ranges from $75,200.00 - $112,790.00 per year . Please note that the offered rate for this position typically aligns with the minimum to midrange of this grade, but it can vary based on the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience, department budget, and an internal equity review. Applicants are encouraged to explore the Professional Staff salary structure and Compensation Guidelines & Policies for more details on Drexel’s compensation framework. For information about benefits, please review Drexel’s Benefits Brochure. Special Instructions
